explain.say: Salmon are born in rivers, grow up at sea and return to the very stream where they hatched to lay their eggs. Their journey home can be over a thousand kilometres.

faq.q: How do salmon find their way back?
faq.a: Out at sea, salmon seem to use Earth's magnetic field as a map to reach the coast near their home river. Then they use smell to pick out their own river and stream.
asks: How do salmon know where to go?

faq.q: How do salmon recognise their home river?
faq.a: Each stream smells slightly different, and young salmon memorise that smell before leaving. In a famous experiment, salmon with blocked noses often failed to choose their home stream.
asks: Do salmon smell their way home?
How do salmon find the exact stream?

faq.q: Why do salmon die after spawning?
faq.a: Pacific salmon stop eating when they enter fresh water and use up all their body's energy on the journey and spawning. Their bodies then feed the stream, bears and forests. Many Atlantic salmon survive and can spawn again.
asks: Do all salmon die after laying eggs?
What happens to salmon after spawning?

faq.q: How can salmon live in both fresh and salt water?
faq.a: Their gills can switch jobs. In fresh water they take in salt and get rid of extra water; in the sea they pump salt out and drink seawater to avoid drying out.
asks: How do salmon change from river to sea?

faq.a: Atlantic salmon can leap waterfalls over 3 metres high, using a powerful burst from the tail, often from a deep pool beneath the fall.
asks: How do salmon get up rivers?

facts: Salmon whose noses were plugged often failed to choose their home stream (Wisby and Hasler, 1954).
Sockeye salmon migration routes matched changes in Earth's magnetic field along the coast (Putman and colleagues, 2013).
